item.title: Gas shortage halts Jamuna Fertilizer Factory again
item.description:
Production at the state-owned Jamuna Fertilizer Company Limited (JFCL) in Sarishabari, Jamalpur, was suspended again on Sunday due to a gas supply shortage, just two days after operations resumed following repairs to a boiler leak.
The shutdown occurred around 5am after Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited and Petrobangla stopped supplying gas to the factory.
The plant resumed production at around 10am on Friday after remaining closed for 15 days to repair the boiler leak. However, officials had warned that inadequate gas pressure could force another shutdown.
The factory has faced repeated disruptions over the past two and a half years due to gas shortages and mechanical problems.
JFCL Additional Chief Engineer (Chemical) Md Fazlul Haque said the factory requires 42-43 million cubic feet of gas daily to maintain uninterrupted urea production.
He said production could resume once gas supply was restored, provided the required pressure was maintained.
The factory has a daily urea production capacity of around 1,700 tonnes and can produce 1,400-1,500 tonnes under favourable operating conditions.
Its urea supplies serve 19 districts, including Jamalpur, Sherpur and Tangail. Prolonged shutdowns could disrupt fertiliser supplies, particularly during the upcoming Boro rice cultivation season, increasing dependence on imports and putting farmers under pressure.

item.title: Dengue: Five more die, 1,546 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Five more people died of dengue and 1,546 new patients were hospitalized across the country in the 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Monday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll in the country has risen to 389 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the new deaths, one each was reported in Dhaka, Chittagong, Khulna, Rajshahi and Barisal divisions.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 126,166 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 119,393 have recovered.

item.title: Sakhawat: Govt plans major expansion of cancer care, radiotherapy facilities
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Monday said the government has taken steps to expand cancer treatment facilities across the country, with procurement of new radiotherapy and robotic surgery equipment underway.
“We are working fast to establish eight cancer institutes in the eight divisions and expand radiotherapy services at district level to ensure cancer treatment at the grassroots,” he said.
The minister made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of the Medical Physics Program at Brac University in the city’s Merul Badda, Dhaka.
The Mathematics and Physical Sciences Department of Brac University introduced the two-year master's program for the first time in Bangladesh to meet the country’s growing demand for medical physicists.
About the government's commitment to ensure treatment for cancer, Sakhawat said the government has planned to procure 17 linear accelerators to make cancer treatment available across the country.
“We are also going to bring five major robotic surgery machines for the first time,” he said, emphasizing early detection and public awareness as critical components of the government’s cancer-control strategy, particularly for breast and cervical cancers.
He said the government would intensify HPV vaccination campaigns and promote breast cancer self-screening and awareness among women.
“Without awareness, we cannot save people from cancer,” Sakhawat said, urging health professionals and educational institutions to help spread awareness at the grassroots level.
Coming down heavily on the previous ‘fascist regime’, he said the ‘previous fascist government’ had destroyed the country’s health sector, which had been marred by corruption and plundering.
However, after assuming office, the present government has taken robust steps for the development of the country’s health sector, he said, adding that once the projects are implemented, the country would witness a revolutionary change in the health sector within the next two years.
“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, we are taking the healthcare services to village level,” the minister said, adding that the government planned to establish Family Wellbeing Centers in every three wards of each union and transform existing community clinics into Health Wellbeing Centers.
“These centers will provide primary-level services, including blood analysis and breast cancer screening,” he said.
Noting that every upazila hospital is going to be transformed into a 150-bed facility, the minister said the government will strengthen dialysis, physiotherapy, and maternal and newborn care at upazila-level hospitals to reduce pressure on tertiary healthcare facilities.
Stating that the government is going to appoint 5,000 doctors soon, Sakhawat said the government is also working to increase the number of hospital beds and recruit around 41,390 health workers, including 25,000 midwives, to strengthen healthcare delivery.
About the newly introduced program at Brac University, he assured government cooperation in developing medical physics education and manpower, saying the government would recruit medical physicists according to the needs of the expanding cancer treatment facilities.
“Medical physics is a very important part of treatment. You do your best and improve yourselves. From the government side, we must extend our hand of cooperation to you,” the minister said.
He said medical physicists play a crucial role in radiotherapy, as the accuracy of radiation dosage is vital for ensuring patient safety and the effectiveness of treatment.
“If the dose is wrong, the patient is gone. If the dose is wrong, the doctor’s credibility is gone,” he said, stressing the need to create adequate numbers of trained medical physicists.
He urged Brac University students, teachers and researchers to contribute to strengthening medical physics and cancer care in Bangladesh.
Professor Emeritus at Dhaka University Dr AFM Yusuf Haider, Additional Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) Professor Dr Jalal Uddin Mohammad Rumi, Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) Clinical Oncology Department Chairman Professor Dr Syed Md Akram Hussain, National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) Director Professor Dr Mostafa Aziz Sumon and Project Director of Establishment of the Integrated Cancer, Kidney and Heart Treatment Centers across Bangladesh's Eight Divisional Cities Dr Md Toufiq Hasan Firoz spoke as special guests at the event.
Brac University Vice-Chancellor Professor Syed Ferhat Anwar chaired the program, while Mathematics and Physical Sciences (MPS) Department Chairperson Professor Hasibun Naher and Registrar and Controller of Examinations of the university Dr David Dowland delivered the welcome address.
Former Director and Chief Medical Physicist at Gummersbach University Hospital, University of Cologne in Germany, and Adviser and Coordinator of MPS at BRAC University, Professor Dr Golam Abu Zakaria presented the keynote paper, while Medical Physics Program Coordinator Professor Hasin Anupama Azhari presented an overview of the newly introduced program.

item.title: Bangladesh to showcase jute products at COP31 in Turkiye
item.description:
The government plans to showcase Bangladesh’s traditional jute and jute-made products at the UN climate conference COP31 in Turkiye to promote them in international markets.
A special exhibition of Bangladeshi jute products is planned at the Bangladesh pavilion during the conference, scheduled to take place in Antalya from November 9 to 20.
The initiative aims to promote jute as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic and highlight the commercial potential of Bangladesh’s jute industry.
Preparations are underway to display a range of jute products and related technologies at the pavilion. An exhibition display has been set up at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as part of the preparations.
The exhibition will showcase products such as jute bags, home décor items and handicrafts to international buyers, investors and policymakers.
Stakeholders believe growing global awareness of environmental pollution and the need for alternatives to plastic presents an opportunity to expand international markets for jute products.
As a natural, renewable and biodegradable fibre, jute has significant potential in environmentally friendly production and consumption.
At a meeting at the Foreign Ministry on October 15, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam highlighted the potential of Bangladesh’s jute industry during discussions on preparations for COP31 with climate experts and relevant stakeholders. The meeting emphasised promoting jute as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic.
If implemented, the initiative could help showcase the diverse uses of jute, explore new markets and strengthen commercial ties with foreign buyers, while bringing Bangladesh’s traditional “golden fibre” industry into the international spotlight.

item.title: UN probe accuses Israel of ‘extermination’ in West Bank
item.description:
Israel has committed the crime against humanity of “extermination” in the West Bank, while continuing to commit “genocide” against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, United Nations-mandated investigators said Monday.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry said Israeli forces had also committed other crimes against humanity and war crimes in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967.
The commission, which does not speak for the UN itself, first determined in a September 2025 report that Israel had committed “genocide” in the war in Gaza following Hamas’ October 7, 2023 resistance campaign on Israel - a finding Israel flatly rejects.
In a new report -- which comes the day before Israel’s general election -- the investigation found that in the West Bank, through military operations reinforced by sustained settler violence, Israel has waged a “widespread and systematic attack” against civilians.
“The Israeli authorities and forces have committed the crimes against humanity of extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence in the West Bank, as well as persecution based on intersecting discriminatory grounds, with nationality, race and ethnicity at its core,” it said.
Israel’s mission in Geneva said the report was part of the inquiry’s “misinformation campaign to demonise the State of Israel and portray its very existence as criminal.”
“The international community must reject these distortions, repudiate the commission’s findings and demand its immediate dissolution,” it said in a statement.
The three-member investigative team was established by the UN Human Rights Council in 2021.
South African former High Court judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the investigation until November 2025, won the Nobel Peace Prize earlier this month.
The commission’s new report focused on killings and bodily and mental harm caused by both Israeli and Palestinian security forces since October 2023.
It found that the situation in the West Bank has deteriorated gravely since the Palestinian fighter group Hamas’s resistance campaign from Gaza that month.
The commission found that the Israeli authorities “intended to collectively punish” West Bank civilians due to the Hamas resistance.
“The targeting of Palestinian civilians across different locations in the West Bank indicates a high level of coordination and organized planning and is the product of state policy,” the report said.
The conduct of Israeli authorities indicates that “they knew and intended settler violence” to be part of the widespread and systematic attack in the West Bank, it added.
“The intentional killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank combined with Israel’s persistent denial of responsibility form part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians and impose conditions of life that are unliveable,” said commission chairman Srinivasan Muralidhar.
“Attempting to equate Palestinian statehood with a threat to the existence of Israel is blocking any viable attempts to realize Palestinians’ right to self-determination,” the Indian judge said in a statement.
The report cited cases where the commission concluded that Israeli forces intended to seriously harm and kill civilians, in acts which amount to war crimes including wilful killing.
Israel’s military offensive, in response, has displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority but whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
“The cases investigated for this report show that the Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” the report said.
The inquiry urged Israel to “end the commission of genocide in Gaza” and act immediately on “obligations to prevent and punish genocide and incitement to genocide.”
Israel should “immediately end the unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory,” and remove all settlers and settlements.
Turning to the Palestinian Authority, the report said that “Palestinian state violence has targeted and continues to target members of opposing Palestinian armed groups and repress Palestinian civil and political opposition.”
The Palestinian Authority struggles with credibility and legitimacy, and “targets Palestinians who voice dissenting civil and political views... resulting in killings,” it said.
“The Palestinian Authority has also failed to conduct prompt, effective and impartial investigations into incidents of killings.”
There was no immediate reaction from the Palestinian Authority.
The commission is due to present its report to the UN General Assembly in New York on Monday.

item.title: e-TIN holders may face Tk5,000 fine for unfiled returns
item.description:
Simply having an e-TIN registration does not mean everyone will face a Tk5,000 fine for failing to submit their income tax return.
According to the Income Tax Act, 2023, penalties are provisioned for failing to submit returns under specific conditions.
However, the amount of the fine depends on whether the taxpayer’s income was previously assessed and which provisions of the law apply to their case.
Recently, information circulated on social media suggesting that failing to submit an income tax return despite having an e-TIN could result in a Tk5,000 fine, causing concern among many.
However, according to the law, for individual taxpayers whose income has never been assessed before, the maximum fine under specified conditions is Tk5,000.
On the other hand, if income has been assessed previously, the calculation for the penalty may differ.
According to data from the National Board of Revenue (NBR), Section 266 of the Income Tax Act, 2023 provides for penalties for failing to submit income tax returns within the stipulated time.
However, this penalty is not automatically imposed on everyone; the respective Deputy Commissioner of Taxes can impose the fine in accordance with the law.
How much is the fine for not submitting a return?
According to Section 266(1) of the Income Tax Act, 2023, if someone fails to submit a return under Section 166, 172, 191, 193, or 212 without a reasonable cause, the respective Deputy Commissioner of Taxes may impose a penalty.
Under the provisions of the law, the fine can be set at 10% of the tax assessed on the latest determined income. In this case, the minimum fine is Tk1,000. If the failure continues, an additional daily penalty of Tk50 is also provisioned.

This means that for individual taxpayers whose income has never been assessed before, Tk5,000 is the maximum penalty ceiling. This is not a predetermined or automatic fine for everyone. The conditions of the law and the taxpayer's situation are taken into consideration when imposing a fine.
Mandatory return submission just because you have an e-TIN?

When is the deadline for submitting income tax returns?
According to general guidelines published by the National Board of Revenue, the standard tax day for natural individual taxpayers is November 30. Returns must be submitted within this period.
However, if the NBR extends the deadline for a specific tax year, that extended deadline applies.
In the past tax year (2025–2026), although the normal deadline was November 30, it was gradually extended, eventually allowing taxpayers to submit returns without penalties up to March 31, 2026.
Failing to submit a return on time should not be neglected.
The applicable tax, additional charges, or penalty for late return submission must be verified.
Calculations may vary depending on the taxpayer's situation and applicable legal provisions.
Income is non-taxable—what should you do?
Many people register for an e-TIN for banking, taking out loans, property registration, or other purposes.
Later, their income might decrease, or they may no longer need those services.
In such situations, it is essential to check whether there is an obligation to submit a return.
You cannot assume that the obligation to submit a return has ended simply because your income has dropped below the tax-free limit or you currently do not owe tax.
If applicable conditions are met, you can apply to the relevant tax authority to cancel your TIN.
However, cancellation depends on the authority's verification and decision.
Canceling a TIN and the obligation to submit a return are two different matters.

Precautions before submitting online returns
When submitting a return, it is crucial to select the correct tax year and accurately provide information on income, investments, assets, and liabilities.
At the same time, details regarding applicable taxes, advance taxes, and tax deducted at source (TDS) must be verified.
Keep acknowledgment receipts or related records after submitting your return. Do not share your NID, TIN, password, or financial information with strangers or on unauthorized websites.
The NBR has issued directives regarding online return submission for natural individual taxpayers in the 2026–27 tax year.
However, approved alternative methods may apply to specific categories of taxpayers and under special circumstances.
If you have an e-TIN but have not submitted your income tax return, you should first check your tax-related status.
There is no need to panic over the Tk5,000 fine information circulated on social media, because under Section 266 of the Income Tax Act, 2023, determining the penalty amount requires considering the taxpayer's previous income assessment, the nature of failure to submit the return, and the applicable conditions of the law.

item.title: Bangladesh's foreign debt repayments increase in Q1 of FY27
item.description:
Bangladesh's External debt servicing has jumped to $1,351.23 million during the 1st quarter (July-September) period of the current FY27.
According to the latest data of the Economic Relations Division (ERD), Bangladesh paid back more than double the foreign assistance it received in actual disbursements during the first quarter (July-September) of FY27.
According to ERD data, external debt servicing costs soared to $1,351.23 million, while foreign aid disbursements reached $662.31 million.
During this July-September period, Bangladesh spent $1.351 billion on principal and interest payments on foreign loans during July-September of FY27, up 5.6% from $1.279 billion in the same period of the previous fiscal year, says the ERD data.
Of the total debt servicing in the first quarter, principal repayments stood at $858.92 million, up from $816.99 million during the corresponding period of FY26.
Interest payments also increased to $492.31 million from $462.96 million a year earlier.
The development partners disbursed $662.31 million in foreign assistance during the first quarter of FY27, down from $1.148 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
Of the total disbursement in July-September this year, $541.74 million came as loans and $120.57 million as grants.
Foreign commitments, however, showed a significant increase.
Development partners committed $1.273 billion in loans and grants during July-September of FY27, up from $910.67 million in the same period of the previous fiscal year - an increase of about 40%.
Of the new commitments, $1.148 billion was in loans, while $125.45 million came in grants.

item.title: IndustriALL seeks Tk32,000 monthly wage for RMG workers
item.description:
The IndustriALL Bangladesh Council has demanded a minimum monthly wage of $260 (Tk32,085 if US$1 is Tk123.41) for the readymade garment (RMG) workers, citing rising living costs.
The council, known as IBC, finalized the demand at an emergency meeting of its central executive committee on Saturday, it said in a press release.
IBC president Mir Abul Kalam Azad presided over the meeting with the present of other leaders.
IBC general secretary Salauddin Swapan said that the meeting discussed the soaring prices of essentials, rise in fuel oil prices and hike of the workers’ transport costs.
Moreover, medical and other living expenses had also increased, making it hard for workers to get by on current wages, he said.
The release added that the 100% to 142% pay rise for government employees had further destabilized the market, deepening the hardship of garment workers and other low-income people.
Taking these factors into account, the committee demanded the $260 minimum wage for garment workers.
IBC said it would soon finalize wage figures for the other grades.
Once a full wage board is formed, it would submit a written proposal to the board’s chairman and the workers’ representative.
The demand comes as the government moves to form a wage board for the sector amid renewed labour protests demanding a monthly minimum wage of Tk30,000.
The Department of Labour, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, has asked garment manufacturers’ and workers’ organizations to nominate representatives for the proposed board.
The department sent separate letters to the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, asking each to nominate three representatives.
The minimum monthly wage for garment workers has risen in successive reviews, from Tk1,662.50 in 2006 to Tk3,000 in 2010, Tk5,300 in 2013, Tk8,000 in 2018, and Tk12,500 in 2023.

item.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.
Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.
Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defense alliance in Mecca in August.
Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.
Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.
“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.
“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”
On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.
The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.
Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.
“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighboring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.
Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy Mena Analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia.”
Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.
“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just... sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.
“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.
“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”
Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.
Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.
On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.
“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.
“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.
The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

item.title: Minister: Bangladeshi workers with expired iqamas to be allowed enter Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Bangladeshi workers whose iqamas (residence permits) expired after they failed to reach Saudi Arabia on time due to flight disruptions will be allowed to enter the kingdom, Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said on Monday.
“Those wishing to go to Saudi Arabia will have their entry formalities completed automatically through the electronic system, and they will be permitted to enter,” he said at a discussion at the BIAM Foundation auditorium on Eskaton Road.
The minister said the target for overseas employment can be achieved if the government and recruiting agencies work together, stressing the need to cut migration costs for workers.
Taking a swipe at recruiting agencies, he said: "Where it is possible to go to Saudi Arabia for Tk3 lakh, charging Tk7-8 lakh is unacceptable. Run your business in a halal way and refrain from extracting excess money from workers, so that they do not spend their entire working time just recovering that cost."
Ariful said modern technology is being introduced at the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) to simplify the overseas-going process and speed up verification of visa authenticity.
A dedicated email service is also being introduced to resolve complaints, he added.
The minister also underscored the need to strictly follow the laws of destination countries and urged recruiting agencies to join the government in conducting necessary awareness campaigns.
Speaking as a special guest, State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Nurul Hoque drew the Saudi government's attention to granting special amnesty to Bangladeshis who currently in jail in the kingdom during the upcoming Ramadan.
He expressed hope that any bilateral issues will be resolved through mutual discussions and called on agencies to lower migration costs.
Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Abdullah ibn Dhafer ibn Ubayya said Bangladeshi workers constitute the largest expatriate community in Saudi Arabia after the country's own nationals.
He said the existing warm ties between the two countries will be further strengthened in the labour sector in the future.
At the meeting, representatives of recruiting agencies demanded simplification of the Takamul test process, a reduction in fees, resolution of BMET's manpower-related complications, and measures to make recruiting agencies stronger and more effective.

Bangladesh, Japan discuss $6.3b private investment in energy, infrastructure, ICT sectors
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan today discussed a proposed private investment of 1 trillion Japanese yen (US$6.3 billion) in Bangladesh’s energy, infrastructure and information and communication technology (ICT) sectors during a bilateral summit between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi.

The two leaders held the summit at the Kantei, the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office, at 11:30 am local time, where they also discussed sending a Japanese team to Bangladesh soon to expedite progress on the proposed investment plan, Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin told BSS.

The talks focused on strengthening the longstanding friendship between the two countries and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, energy security, technology, space research, infrastructure development and regional and international affairs.

During the meeting, Tarique Rahman called on the Japanese government and private sector to play a more active role in Bangladesh’s economic development, technological advancement and industrialisation.

Highlighting the government’s vision of transforming Bangladesh into a hub for economic activity, technology and manufacturing, the Prime Minister said the country could become the world’s ninth-largest consumer economy by 2030, while its gross domestic product (GDP) could exceed US$1 trillion by 2034.

He said Japan holds a special place in the hearts of the people of Bangladesh, recalling that it was among the first countries to recognise Bangladesh after its independence in 1971 and had since remained one of the country’s key development partners.

The relationship between the two countries, he said, was built on mutual respect, trust and shared aspirations for peace, prosperity and stability.
Emphasising Bangladesh’s energy security, Tarique Rahman said reliable and affordable energy supplies were essential to sustaining the country’s economic growth.

He expressed gratitude for Japan’s longstanding support in the energy sector and called for greater Japanese investment and participation in Bangladesh’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, efficient power generation and renewable energy.

Referring to a recent 50-billion-yen emergency assistance loan under the Partnership for Power Asia initiative to strengthen energy security in Asia, the prime minister highlighted opportunities to expand cooperation in the sector.

To help build a research- and technology-driven economy, Tarique Rahman proposed establishing a Bangladesh-Japan Tech Park to connect Japanese companies, universities and investors with Bangladesh’s young talent, entrepreneurs and skilled technology professionals.

He suggested prioritising artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, robotics and electronics manufacturing at the proposed facility.

The Prime Minister also expressed interest in expanding cooperation with Japan in space science, satellite engineering and related technologies, drawing on Japan’s advanced capabilities in these fields.

Highlighting the need for modern and integrated transport infrastructure, he outlined plans to establish a high-speed rail network connecting six major divisional cities and build elevated roads across the country.

He sought Japan’s cooperation in planning, providing technical assistance, investing in and financing such large-scale infrastructure projects.

Tarique Rahman said his government was committed to improving the investment climate through reforms to regulatory systems, tax policies, customs clearance and fund-transfer procedures.

He expressed hope that the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), signed in February 2026, would be implemented promptly.

He proposed establishing a joint ministerial commission to identify priority areas, accelerate implementation and translate opportunities for cooperation into concrete initiatives, while underscoring the importance of closer engagement between the two countries’ business communities.
The Bangladesh premier also invited Takaichi to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time.

Following the summit, the two leaders made a joint press announcement on the outcomes of their discussions and exchanged several memorandums of understanding in key areas. Takaichi also hosted an official luncheon in honour of Tarique Rahman at the Kantei.

The Bangladesh premier arrived in Tokyo on Monday for a four-day official visit at the invitation of Takaichi. During the visit, he is also scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum and meet Japanese business leaders.

item.title: Dengue death toll reaches 400; October deadliest month
item.description:
Dengue has claimed 11 more lives in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, taking the death toll this year to 400. Of these, 155 people have died in the first 27 days of October alone, while 2,071 new patients have been hospitalised during the same period.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) disclosed the figures in its daily report on Tuesday.
According to the report, 899 of the newly hospitalised patients were from Dhaka division, the highest among the country's eight divisions. Khulna recorded 250 admissions, followed by Chittagong with 241, Rajshahi with 229, Barisal with 217, Rangpur with 112, Mymensingh with 97 and Sylhet with 26.
DGHS data show that dengue fatalities remained relatively low during the first five months of the year. Two people died in each of January and February, while no deaths were recorded in March or April. One person died in May.
The death toll rose to 13 in June, 36 in July and 43 in August before surging to 148 in September. In the first 27 days of October, the disease claimed another 155 lives.
September and October together accounted for 303 deaths, more than 75% of the year's total. By comparison, 97 people died of dengue in the first eight months of the year, highlighting a sharp rise in fatalities in recent months.
October's death toll has already surpassed September's total, with five days still remaining in the month.
Tuesday's report also recorded the highest number of dengue deaths in a single day this year, with 11 fatalities reported in the preceding 24 hours.
The previous highest daily toll was 10, recorded on October 6 and October 15.
According to the DGHS, a total of 128,237 dengue patients were hospitalised across the country between January 1 and 8:00am on October 27. Of them, 121,422 have recovered and been discharged, while 6,415 remain under treatment at hospitals nationwide.
The sharp rise in fatalities in September and October, coupled with the continued admission of thousands of patients, underscores the growing severity of the dengue outbreak across Bangladesh.
Medicine specialist Dr ABM Abdullah has stressed the need to destroy Aedes mosquito breeding sites and eliminate adult mosquitoes to curb dengue transmission.
He said the authorities should conduct regular cleanliness drives, while individuals must also take precautions to protect themselves from mosquito bites.
Some dengue patients are experiencing rapid deterioration, with some developing severe complications and going into shock within just one or two days, he said, urging people not to ignore a fever and to seek medical advice promptly.
Dr Abdullah advised extra caution if children, older people, pregnant women, and patients with cancer or liver disease develop a fever.
He also emphasised the importance of adequate fluid intake for dengue patients. Those experiencing vomiting, difficulty eating or diarrhoea should seek medical attention without delay.
He warned against taking painkillers purchased from pharmacies without consulting a doctor when experiencing a fever.
According to Dr Abdullah, early treatment improves the chances of recovery, while delays in seeking medical care can make severe cases, particularly those involving shock, more difficult to manage. Patients with underlying health conditions face additional risks, he added.
Dr Muhammad Nurul Islam, deputy director of Mugda Medical College Hospital, said people are exposed to different dengue virus variants each year. A second dengue infection could be one possible reason for the rapid deterioration in the condition of some children, he added.
He stressed that people should take dengue symptoms seriously even before the infection is confirmed. Patients should be closely monitored and take medication and undergo necessary tests as advised by a physician, he said.

item.title: Dhaka, Tokyo to upgrade BIG-B into ‘BIG-B for Shared Prosperity’
item.description:
In light of the rapidly changing global situation, a more prevalent supply chain risk, rapid technological innovation and mounting social issues, Bangladesh and Japan will upgrade BIG-B into “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity” as an initiative of “strategic cooperation” in the exclusive partnership between the two countries.
This is aimed at enhancing the resilience and preserving each country’s freedom of decision, said the Japanese government.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh and Japan signed a number of Memoranda of Cooperation and other documents between the two countries, said the Japanese side.
The two countries signed five cooperation documents covering economic relations and the business environment, agriculture, fisheries and livestock, and environmental protection.
These include a memorandum of cooperation between Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Bangladesh’s Economic Relations Division; separate memoranda between Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock; a memorandum of cooperation on the environment between Japan’s Ministry of the Environment and Bangladesh’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; and a letter of intent between Japan’s Global Environment Bureau and Bangladesh’s Department of Environment under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
BIG-B (the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt) is an economic development initiative with three pillars: (1) economic infrastructure development, (2) improvement of the investment environment, (3) strengthening connectivity.
It has served as the flagship initiative of Japan-Bangladesh cooperation and has long supported Bangladesh’s economic growth.
The “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity” positions Bangladesh as a hub to promote common prosperity and to contribute to mutual growth, said the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Japan and Bangladesh have agreed to strengthen cooperation in connectivity, energy security, disaster resilience, trade, investment and defence to promote economic growth and regional peace and stability.
Under the proposed cooperation framework, the two countries will promote integrated economic infrastructure development centred on Matarbari Deep-Sea Port, including power and energy facilities, airports, roads, railways, inland waterways and special economic zones, to strengthen supply chains and develop Bangladesh into a logistics and industrial hub.
They will also work to improve the investment climate, develop human resources, expand public-private partnerships and establish transparent and predictable rules to attract investment.
Both sides will seek to expand trade and investment under the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), improve market access and promote industrial upgrading and export diversification.
The cooperation will also focus on building resilient supply chains in manufacturing, logistics, food and agriculture, information and communication technology, pharmaceuticals and other sectors.
To strengthen energy security, the two countries will promote initiatives under Japan's “POWERR Asia” framework for a stable and economically viable energy supply and explore opportunities for energy infrastructure development in the Matarbari region.
They will also enhance cooperation to address natural disasters and climate change, including strengthening emergency response capabilities and developing sustainable disaster-prevention infrastructure.
In the security sector, Japan will support Bangladesh's capacity-building efforts and promote bilateral security and defence cooperation, with a focus on maritime security, maritime domain awareness, coastal patrols and port security.
The framework includes providing patrol boats to Bangladesh under Japan's first Official Security Assistance (OSA) project, exploring a second OSA project and providing patrol vessels through official development assistance (ODA) to strengthen coastal security capabilities.
Both countries will also work to improve their ability to respond to emerging technological challenges, including cybersecurity, as part of broader efforts to enhance resilience against geopolitical uncertainties and promote peace and stability.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen bilateral relations under the two countries’ Strategic Partnership, with a focus on regional peace, prosperity and stability.
At a summit meeting in Japan, Takaichi congratulated Tarique Rahman on assuming office as prime minister and described Bangladesh as a friend that shares the values of democracy.
Amid growing international instability, she said Japan strongly supports Bangladesh’s ability to make its own decisions freely and strengthen its resilience under Japan’s updated “Free and Open Indo-Pacific” (FOIP) vision.
Takaichi also expressed her intention to work with Tarique Rahman to promote peace and prosperity in the region.
In response, Tarique Rahman said Japan, as a peace-loving nation, was among the first countries to recognise Bangladesh’s independence and holds a special place in the hearts of the Bangladeshi people.
He said the two countries had built longstanding friendly relations and expressed his commitment to working with Takaichi to take bilateral ties to new heights.
The two leaders held the summit meeting on October 27 from 11:45am for around 25 minutes, followed by a joint press event and luncheon, according to the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iran says supreme leader met with security chief over Hormuz
item.description:
Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since he took office in March, has met with security chief Mohsen Rezaei to discuss regional security and the Strait of Hormuz, his office said Tuesday.
Mojtaba was chosen in March to succeed his father and longtime ruler Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in US-Israeli strikes on February 28 in central Tehran alongside senior military commanders, and was said to have been injured in the same attack.
He has only communicated through written messages since his appointment, some of them published in handwriting attributed to him.
During the meeting, the first publicly announced encounter between Rezaei and the leader, they discussed “strengthening bilateral relations with neighboring countries” and “safeguarding national and regional security through the management of the Strait of Hormuz,” Khamenei’s office said in a statement.
Khamenei “emphasized the need to safeguard the rights and interests of the Iranian nation and the resistance front by adhering to the conditions set by the country’s authorities, with the aim of ending the war and the state of neither war nor peace,” it added.
Their meeting was announced a day after Rezaei held talks with senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan -- countries which recently signed the mutual defense Mecca Pact.
Neither the date nor the location of the meeting was disclosed.
Iran claims control over the Hormuz strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorization, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.
Several Iranian officials, including Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, have in recent days said they held rare meetings with the supreme leader.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,240 as 7 die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children died with measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to 8am on Tuesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,240 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified six latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths while another as a confirmed measles death.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,136, while confirmed deaths from measles stood at 105.
A total of 1,232 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 223,784.
Meanwhile, 63 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 23,541.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 199,127 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 191,090 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: IRRI, govt move to strengthen methane emissions monitoring in rice production
item.description:
The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) has brought together government agencies, researchers and development partners in Dhaka for a two-day workshop aimed at strengthening Bangladesh’s capacity to measure, report and verify greenhouse gas emissions from rice cultivation.
The workshop, held on October 27–28, focuses on developing a national measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) system and advancing a methane mitigation roadmap for the rice sector.
Organized under the Accelerating the Scaling of Low-emissions Rice Production in Southeast Asia (AcceLER) project and CGIAR’s Climate Action and Scaling for Impact science programs, the event seeks to improve emissions tracking and institutional coordination.
Rice cultivation supports approximately 13 million farming households in Bangladesh but is also a major source of agricultural methane emissions.
Addressing the workshop, Agriculture Secretary Md Salim Khan emphasized the need to reduce emissions without compromising food security or farmers’ livelihoods.
“What we cannot measure, we cannot manage,” he said, adding that a transparent MRV system would strengthen Bangladesh’s greenhouse gas inventory and reporting under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), while creating opportunities for climate finance.
Department of Agricultural Extension Director General Md Abdur Rahim stressed the importance of reliable data systems for expanding climate-smart agricultural practices and accessing international climate finance.
Bangladesh Rice Research Institute Director General Dr Md Rafiqul Islam said the proposed MRV system must be cost-effective, scalable and transparent.
He identified alternate wetting and drying (AWD), climate-smart rice varieties, improved fertilizer management, direct-seeded rice and better residue management as potential measures to reduce emissions.
IRRI Bangladesh Country Representative Dr Humnath Bhandari highlighted the potential of digital MRV systems to provide reliable emissions data at farm, project and national levels.
IRRI Senior Scientist Dr Bjoern Ole Sander said research had identified practical approaches to reducing emissions from rice production, emphasizing methane’s contribution to global warming and ground-level ozone formation.
Technical discussions examined existing agricultural reporting systems, institutional responsibilities, data gaps and a proposed national MRV framework.
Participants also reviewed experiences from Cambodia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam in promoting low-emission rice cultivation.
The workshop includes practical greenhouse gas quantification exercises using IRRI tools, alongside discussions on remote sensing, digital data management and institutional requirements.
Organizers said the initiative aims to support Bangladesh in developing a coordinated, science-based system for monitoring agricultural emissions and implementing low-emission rice production practices.

item.title: Foreign aid commitments rise 40% in Q1 of FY27
item.description:
Foreign loan and grant commitments to Bangladesh rose by nearly 40% in the first quarter (July-September) of the current FY27.
Development partners committed $1.273 billion in loans and grants during the July-September period, up from $910.67 million in the same period of the previous fiscal year, marking a year-on-year increase of 39.8%, according to the latest data from the Economic Relations Division (ERD).
Of the total commitments received during the first three months of FY27, loans accounted for $1.14758 billion, while grants amounted to $125.45 million.
The increase in new commitments could create opportunities for additional foreign financing for development projects in the coming months.
However, the actual availability of the funds will depend on disbursement schedules, project readiness and fulfilment of relevant conditions.
Meanwhile, a major foreign financing initiative is underway for the modernization and expansion of Eastern Refinery Limited, the country's sole oil refinery.
The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) has committed around $1 billion to the project.
If implemented, the financing is expected to help increase the country's oil-refining capacity and strengthen energy security.
Despite the rise in new commitments, actual foreign aid disbursements declined during the quarter.
Development partners disbursed $662.31 million in foreign assistance in July-September of FY27, down from $1.14859 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
Of the total assistance disbursed in the first quarter, project aid amounted to $652.31 million, comprising $541.74 million in loans and $110.57 million in grants.
Another $10 million was disbursed as food aid in the form of grants.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh spent $1.35123 billion on repaying the principal and interest of foreign loans during the first quarter of FY27, compared with $1.27995 billion in the same period a year earlier, representing an increase of 5.6%.
According to ERD data, the country repaid $858.92 million in foreign loan principal during July-September, up from $816.99 million in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year.
Interest payments also increased to $492.31 million during the quarter from $462.96 million a year earlier.
Foreign aid commitments represent pledges of future financing by development partners, while disbursements refer to funds actually released for projects and programs.
Ensuring timely disbursement of committed funds and their effective utilization in development projects remains crucial alongside the increase in new commitments.

item.title: IMF: Bangladesh to surpass India in per capita GDP this year
item.description:
Bangladesh is projected to overtake neighbouring India in nominal per capita gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026, with its per capita GDP expected to reach $2,886, compared with $2,749 for India, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook projects Bangladesh's per capita GDP to exceed India's by $137 this year, marking a reversal of the trend in recent years, when India moved ahead of Bangladesh on this measure.
Per capita GDP is calculated by dividing a country's total economic output by its population.
Bangladesh has made significant economic progress over the past two decades, driven largely by the expansion of its readymade garment (RMG) industry, strong remittance inflows and increased participation of women in the labour force.

item.title: HSC results delayed, new date set for October 31
item.description:
The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than the previously announced date.
The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee had earlier set October 29 for the publication of the results. The date was revised due to a change in the venue for the official result announcement.
Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee Chairman and Dhaka Education Board Chairman Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman confirmed the decision on Tuesday.
He told Dhaka Tribune that the venue was changed following complaints from journalists about inadequate space at the Secretariat during last year’s result publication ceremony.
“Last year, journalists complained about the lack of space at the Secretariat on the day the results were published. We informed the education minister, who considered the matter and agreed to change the venue. Accordingly, the results will be formally published at the International Mother Language Institute on Saturday,” he said.
Earlier, the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee had proposed publishing the results between October 25 and 29. Based on the proposal, October 29 was initially fixed as the publication date.
The HSC and equivalent examinations under nine general education boards, the Bangladesh Technical Education Board and the Bangladesh Madrasah Education Board began across the country on July 2.
The exams were scheduled to end on August 8, but examinations under several boards, including the Chittagong Education Board, took longer to complete due to flooding.
A total of 12,70,583 candidates appeared for the HSC, Alim, HSC (BM-BMT), HSC (Vocational) and Diploma-in-Commerce examinations under 11 education boards. The exams were held at 2,697 centres involving 9,439 institutions.
This year, the nine general education boards conducted the examinations using common question papers.
The 2026 HSC and equivalent examinations began on July 2 and ended on August 8, while the practical examinations were completed by August 15.

item.title: Third uranium shipment reaches Rooppur plant under tight security
item.description:
The third shipment of nuclear fuel, weighing 41 tons, has reached the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Ishwardi, Pabna, amid tight security.
The vehicles carrying the fuel entered the plant premises around 8am on Tuesday under military escort.
The shipment arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on a special flight from Russia on Monday morning, following a stopover in Delhi, India. The fuel was packed into 12 transport containers.
In the early hours of Tuesday, the containers were loaded onto three lorries and transported by road to Rooppur. The convoy crossed the Bangabandhu Bridge and passed through Bonpara in Natore and Dashuria in Ishwardi before reaching the project site.
Police personnel were stationed at several intersections along the route to manage traffic. Members of the military, the Special Security Force (SSF) and intelligence agencies were also involved in security arrangements.
According to police and project sources, the fuel was transported from Dhaka under a special security protocol. Traffic movement along parts of the highway was temporarily restricted to prevent congestion during the convoy's passage.
Project officials said 163 uranium fuel assemblies for the plant's second unit were scheduled to arrive in seven shipments. Another 48 assemblies for refuelling the first unit were expected in two shipments. The latest consignment is the third shipment for the second unit.
Seven more flights carrying fuel from Russia are planned for November and December. The shipments are expected to transit through Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India.
Russia's state nuclear energy corporation, Rosatom, has said the fuel supply process is expected to be completed by December.
Fuel for the plant's first unit arrived in Bangladesh on September 29, 2023, followed by four additional shipments in October and November that year. Fuel loading in the first unit's reactor was completed in May this year.
The first unit will require the replacement of about one-fourth of its fuel after approximately 18 months of operation. A shipment of additional fuel for the unit arrived at Rooppur on October 3, while the second shipment for the second unit reached the project site on October 21.
Under the agreement, Russia will supply fuel for the plant during its first three years of operation. Bangladesh will then need to import fuel for periodic replacement.
The Rooppur plant comprises two units with a combined generation capacity of 2,400MW. Although fuel loading in the first unit has been completed, electricity generation has been delayed by technical complications.
Power generation had been expected to begin this month but was postponed following a fault in a safety valve in the automatic pressure relief system. A third round of testing on the valve was completed on September 30, and project officials began the nuclear reaction process on October 11 after receiving regulatory approval, according to project sources.
Sources said the necessary tests and procedures for the first unit, including the B-2 phase of physics testing, were completed this week. The reports have been submitted to the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) for review.
After receiving final approval, the unit is expected to move to Stage C, or power startup, a key phase before electricity generation. During this stage, the plant's systems will undergo comprehensive testing to verify their functionality.

item.title: UN: Greenhouse gas levels hit new record highs in 2025
item.description:
Greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere rose to new record highs in 2025, locking in climate impacts that will persist for centuries to come, the United Nations said Tuesday.
Levels of the three main greenhouse gases -- the climate-warming carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide -- all rose to unprecedented figures in 2025, the UN’s weather and climate agency said.
The World Meteorological Organization said the rise would lead to more long-term temperature increases for the planet.
The WMO’s 22nd annual Greenhouse Gas Bulletin comes ahead of the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, running from November 9 to 20.
“Another year, another new record,” said WMO deputy secretary-general Ko Barrett.
“Greenhouse gases are trapping an unprecedented amount of heat in the atmosphere, providing energy for more extreme weather and associated risks to our economies and societies.
“The past 11 years have been the warmest on record and this trend is set to continue. Carbon dioxide (CO2) has a very long life-time and so will affect the global climate not just for years but for decades and even centuries.”
The bulletin looks at greenhouse gas concentrations -- the amount of those gases in the atmosphere -- rather than new annual emissions amounts as the world burns more coal, oil and gas.
In 2025, carbon dioxide concentrations were at 426.8 parts per million (ppm); methane at 1,948 parts per billion, and nitrous oxide at 339.1 parts per billion.
That takes them respectively to 153%, 267% and 126% of the pre-industrial levels witnessed before 1750.
Of the three major greenhouse gases, CO2 accounts for about 66 percent of the warming effect on the climate.
Around half of the total CO2 emitted each year remains in the atmosphere; the rest is absorbed by the land and oceans.
From 2024 to 2025, the global average concentration of CO2 rose by 2.8 ppm -- smaller than the record surge from 2023 to 2024 of 3.6 ppm.
WMO senior scientific officer Oksana Tarasova said this reflected the “recovery of the land carbon sinks and reduced fire carbon emissions in 2025 after the strong 2023/2024 El Nino,” the naturally occurring, climate-warming weather phenomenon.
“However, a 2.8 ppm annual increase is still a substantial addition of carbon to the atmosphere from fossil fuel burning.”
It is also above the average growth rate for the past decade of 2.6 ppm -- a figure that stood at 0.8 ppm in the 1960s.
“We can expect to see a further increase in concentrations in 2026 because of fossil fuel burning and the development of a powerful El Nino which will impact land carbon sinks, as it did in 2023/2024,” Tarasova warned.
Methane accounts for about 16 percent of the warming effect on our climate by long-lived greenhouse gases, though it has a much shorter lifetime than CO2.
Around a third of methane emitted into the atmosphere comes from natural sources like wetlands, with the rest from anthropogenic sources such as cattle, rice farming, landfills and biomass burning.
The bulletin said that as countries shift their energy systems towards decarbonization, more attention should be paid to two potent but less abundant trace gases closely related to electricity production and distribution: molecular hydrogen (H2) and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).
Primarily as a spark suppressant in electricity distribution, SF6 has been rising steadily over the past three decades.
Why H2 levels have increased over the past decade is unknown but it has begun to be used as an energy storage medium.

item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today sought Japan’s cooperation in diversifying Bangladesh’s export products, expressing hope that stronger economic ties would open up new avenues for trade and investment between the two countries.

He sought Japan’s cooperation during a meeting with Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) President Susumu Kataoka here at 11:45 am local time, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin.

During the meeting, the discussions focused on increasing Japanese investment in Bangladesh, diversifying exports, developing skills and strengthening bilateral trade and economic partnership.

Tarique Rahman appreciated JETRO’s role in promoting Japanese investment in Bangladesh, saying, “New opportunities for Japanese investment are emerging in Bangladesh.”

He said Bangladesh expected Japanese investment in manufacturing industries, information and communication technology (ICT), automobiles, renewable energy and agro-processing in the country’s special economic zones.

Both sides agreed that the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) would play an important role in strengthening trade and investment ties between the two countries.

The Prime Minister also urged Japan to cooperate in skills development programmes and the establishment of Japanese language training centres in Bangladesh. Such initiatives would help create employment opportunities in Japan and further strengthen the long-term economic partnership between the two countries, said the premier.

JETRO President Susumu Kataoka described Bangladesh as a promising investment destination, citing its economic growth and geographical location.

He said various initiatives taken by the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had already generated interest among Japanese companies in doing business and investing in Bangladesh.

Following the meeting, the Prime Minister attended a luncheon hosted by Kataoka. They also discussed ways to advance mutual cooperation and economic relations.

Tarique Rahman invited the JETRO president to visit Bangladesh at a time convenient to him.

Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M. item.title: Metro rail: Formal work kicks off for stations, tracks construction of 2 new routes
item.description:
Eight elevated stations and 11 kilometers of elevated tracks will be constructed for two new metro rail lines under four packages.

Contractors have been appointed for the construction of stations and railway tracks for MRT Line-1 (from the capital's Airport to Kamalapur) and MRT Line-5 (Northern Route, from Hemayetpur to Bhatara).

Additionally, various depot infrastructures will also be developed in Hemayetpur and Purbachal. The appointment of contractors marks the formal commencement of the construction of these stations and railway tracks.

Contracts under the four separate packages were signed on Tuesday (27 October) afternoon at the Metro Rail Bhaban in Diabari, Uttara. The two projects are being implemented by Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL) with joint financing from the Bangladesh government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).

The total cost for constructing these two metro rail lines will be Tk 2 trillion. Of this, Tk 1.14 trillion will be spent on MRT Line-1 and Tk 890 billion on MRT Line-5.

MRT Line-1 will be 31 kilometers long, while MRT Line-5 will span 20 kilometers.

The metro rail line from Airport to Kamalapur will have 21 stations. The line from Hemayetpur to Bhatara will have 14 stations. Construction of both lines is scheduled to be completed by 2033.

Mohammad Ziaul Haque, secretary of the Road Transport and Highways Division attended the contract signing ceremony as the chief guest. Planning Commission Member (Acting Secretary) Kabir Ahmed was present as the special guest.

DMTCL Managing Director Md. Shaugatul Alam, along with representatives from the Embassy of Japan, JICA, project officials, consultants and contracting firms, were also present on the occasion, DMTCL said in a press release.

Works under 4 packages

According to the DMTCL press release, a total of 49 structures will be constructed for the MRT Line-1 depot under the agreement. This will include workshops, stabling sheds and an operation management centre.

The contract for this work was signed with China's Sinohydro and SEBCL. In addition, the contract for constructing a five-kilometre elevated viaduct and three stations (Joar Sahara, Boalia and Mastul) on this line was signed with China's CREC and MBEC and Japan's MIL.

For the MRT Line-5 depot, an agreement was signed with Taiwan's CPC and South Korea's Hanil to construct various infrastructures, including an administrative building, stabling yard, warehouse and workshop sheds.

Under another package, a contract was signed with CREC-MIL-MBEC for constructing a total of 6.50 kilometers of elevated railway from Hemayetpur to Aminbazar and from Natun Bazar to Bhatara, alongside five stations: Hemayetpur, Baliyapur, Bilamalia, Aminbazar and Bhatara.

The press release stated that implementing these four packages will advance the expansion of the capital's metro rail infrastructure.

Speaking at the ceremony, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Mohammad Ziaul Haque said that easing traffic congestion and reducing commute times in Dhaka remain one of the government's top priorities. To this end, the metro rail network is being expanded to build a modern, safe, and environmentally friendly mass transit system.

item.title: PM invites Japanese firms to explore five sectors for investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today invited Japanese companies to explore investment opportunities in five priority sectors in Bangladesh-automotive manufacturing, energy, technology and space cooperation, rail and logistics, and agro-processing and manufacturing-to translate long standing bilateral ties into stronger trade and investment.

"I invite Japanese companies to explore five key areas for future cooperation and business opportunities for mutual benefits," he said while delivering the keynote speech at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue at JETRO Hall in Tokyo.

Highlighting the untapped potential of bilateral economic ties, the Prime Minister said around 350 Japanese companies operate in Bangladesh, while Japanese direct investment in the country remains below US$500 million.

"Our exports to Japan reached 1.36 billion US dollars and Bangladesh imported from Japan 2.16 billion US dollars, in the last fiscal year," he said, stressing the need to take the relationship beyond development cooperation and expand trade and investment.

Recalling the longstanding friendship between the two countries, Rahman said Japan was among the first countries to recognise Bangladesh in February 1972 and had remained its largest development partner for more than five decades.

He also recalled the contributions of his parents-- Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and late Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia-- who visited Japan several times and helped deepen bilateral relations.

"Today, I want to speak about the next 30-50 years of partnership and collaboration," he said.

Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh and Japan had signed an Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) this year, the first such agreement Bangladesh had concluded with any country. Under the agreement, 7,379 Bangladeshi products will enjoy duty-free access to Japan, while Japanese goods, including steel, automotive parts and electronic components, will receive preferential access to Bangladesh.

The Prime Minister highlighted Bangladesh''s market of more than 180 million people, its young and energetic workforce with a median age of 27, and its growing middle class as major advantages for investors.

He said Bangladesh was expected to become one of the world''s top 10 consumer economies by 2030.

Identifying automotive manufacturing as the first priority, Tarique Rahman welcomed Toyota's plan, conveyed earlier this month, to begin work on a vehicle manufacturing facility in Bangladesh, with full production targeted by 2029. He assured the company of the government's full support.

In the energy sector, he invited Japanese companies to invest in liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, efficient gas-fired power generation and renewable energy.

He said Bangladesh had short-, medium- and long-term plans for gas, electricity and the wider energy sector, and urged Japanese firms to explore the opportunities, noting that Bangladesh was working closely with JERA.

On technology and space cooperation, the premier said Bangladesh was planning to establish a Bangladesh-Japan Technology Park, including an innovation-focused information technology park covering artificial intelligence, cloud computing, robotics and electronics manufacturing, with the involvement of Japanese companies, universities and investors.

He said the two countries also had significant potential for cooperation in space technology. Bangladesh wanted to strengthen its space capabilities and was keen to explore mutually beneficial collaboration with Japanese institutions, drawing on Japan's experience in space science, technology and satellite engineering.

The Prime Minister identified rail and logistics as another priority, saying Bangladesh planned to build a nationwide elevated high-speed rail network connecting major cities, including Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Rajshahi, Khulna and Barishal.

"We plan to build a national network master plan, develop passenger and freight demand analysis, route prioritisation and feasibility studies. We will very much welcome Japanese institutions to invest in this critical and priority initiative," he said.

In agro-processing and manufacturing, the Prime Minister invited Japanese companies to explore food-processing opportunities in Bangladesh, which produces a wide variety of crops, fruits and vegetables.

"Japanese companies can explore opportunities in food processing in Bangladesh. We invite Japanese companies to invest in the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone at Araihazar. Sumitomo Corporation is developing this zone to Japanese standards," he said.

The Prime Minister said Bangladesh was working to address concerns raised by Japanese companies about reliable energy, efficient infrastructure, and predictable customs clearance and taxation.
"We have listened. We are working to address these concerns and deliver better outcomes," he said, adding, "I fully understand that businesses need certainty. Investors need confidence. Our job is creating the right environment to deliver both."

Emphasising people-to-people ties and skills development, Tarique Rahman said Bangladeshi students travelled to Japan every year for higher education, gaining valuable skills and experience before returning home.
He said teaching Japanese to Bangladeshi students was a government priority and outlined a vision of millions of young people learning the Japanese language alongside technical skills.

The premier said highly skilled Bangladeshi professionals with Japanese-language proficiency could help meet employment needs in both Japan and Bangladesh.

"Japan stood beside Bangladesh as we built our foundations. Now, we invite you to build our industries, create new opportunities, and grow together," he said.

The premier added, "Let us turn our longstanding friendship into a stronger partnership. Let us create mutual opportunities for our people, and prosperity for both of our nations."

The Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue was organised by the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) in cooperation with the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Co-operation (JBCCEC), with support from the Bangladesh Embassy in Japan.

JETRO President Susumu Kataoka delivered the opening remarks, while Japan''s Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Shinji Wakayama addressed the event as a guest speaker. The programme also featured an MoU exchange ceremony and announcements of investment and cooperation projects.

Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury spoke on building an investment-led economy in Bangladesh, while Invest Bangladesh Chairman Ashik Chowdhury presented reforms and new initiatives to facilitate investment in Bangladesh.

Kenichiro Kawamoto, branch general manager and country chairperson of Mitsui & Co. (Asia Pacific) Pte. Ltd.''s Dhaka branch, delivered a presentation titled "Together for a Brighter Bangladesh". Reisuke Aratani, vice-president of YKK Corporation''s Global Sales Headquarters, presented the company''s business journey in Bangladesh and its future prospects.
Prime Minister''s Adviser Rehan Asif Asad also spoke on high-growth emerging businesses in Bangladesh.

Sakhawat makes surprise visit to Comilla hospital, orders action against five doctors
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Wednesday ordered departmental action against five doctors for failing to join their assigned workplaces for an extended period after their appointment, during a surprise visit to Muradnagar Upazila Health Complex in Comilla.
The minister visited the hospital without prior notice this morning and inspected its medical services and overall activities.
During the visit, he toured the hospital wards, emergency department, and outpatient department. He also spoke directly with patients and their attendants to learn about the quality of healthcare services, availability of medicines, and any difficulties they were facing.
The minister immediately instructed the Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to take departmental action against the five doctors who had not joined their workplaces despite their appointments.
He also closely examined the hospital's cleanliness and checked whether doctors and other healthcare workers were attending their duties regularly and performing their responsibilities properly.
Speaking to journalists and the authorities concerned after the inspection, Sakhawat Husain said ensuring quality healthcare service at people’s doorsteps is a top priority of the current government.
He stressed that no patient should be deprived of treatment at government hospitals or subjected to harassment by brokers.
The minister urged hospital authorities to remain highly vigilant to prevent such harassment and ensure that patients receive proper medical care. He also described regular attendance by doctors and maintaining cleanliness as mandatory.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,242 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,242.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified both of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,137, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The two new suspected fatalities were reported across two divisions; Dhaka and Sylhet with one death each.
A total of 1,322 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 225,106.
During the same period, 90 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,631.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 200,319 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 192,178 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.
